reference_images.role: Established nara desktop chrome, local docking tabs and project atmosphere
Established component styles, color, typography and density

notes: These are proposed editor UI designs, not screenshots of an implemented engine.
Profiler data, waveform, traces and simulation values are illustrative; exact behavior is specified in the Markdown and JSON token file.
SVG is used only for the retained brand assets. All ten new editor references are generated raster images.

images.initial_prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create a new high-fidelity raster component atlas for the nara game editor, matching the supplied nara graphite reference in density, materials, compact desktop typography and turquoise accents. Landscape 3:2 composition, straight-on, very crisp, practically usable controls. Small heading: 'nara / property editors' and 'Graphite · 0.4'. The sheet contains six clearly separated independent specimens in a tight 3-column by 2-row grid; thin dividers and restrained 4px corners, no large web cards. Each specimen has realistic property rows and compact controls, not decorative rectangles.

Top left: '01 Multi-object editing'. An Inspector header '3 objects · Edit world'. Transform rows: Position X '—', Y '0.00', Z '—'; Rotation X '0.0°', Y '—', Z '0.0°'; Scale 1.00 on each axis, with an explicit unlinked scale icon. Colored X/Y/Z letters remain readable. An indeterminate 'Visible' checkbox and a small explanation 'Mixed values'. A Light section reads '2 of 3 objects' with a separate 'Add to missing' action.

Top middle: '02 Field states'. Separate, labeled rows for normal value, keyboard focus, source override, invalid input, readonly, and disabled. Use an intact focused teal outline, a blue source marker beside 'Intensity 4.00' with 'Source: 2.00', a pink outlined numeric buffer '12..5' with 'Enter a valid number', and a readable lock-marked asset ID with a Copy icon. A disabled action has a short visible reason. Footer distinguishes source override from 'Unsaved document' using two different symbols.

Top right: '03 Choices & structure'. A 'Shadow mode' enum dropdown open with None, Hard, Soft and Soft selected. Below, independent specimen of flags 'Collision layers' showing Player checked, World checked, Trigger empty, with Apply and Cancel. A compact 'Waypoints · 3' ordered list has three named entries, index labels, drag handles, expand arrows, Add and Remove controls.

Bottom left: '04 References'. Five distinct AssetField rows, each labeled: Assigned 'beacon_mesh', Empty 'Choose mesh…', Missing 'arch_old.mesh' with warning and Locate, Pending 'arch_lod.mesh' with a small spinner and 'Importing', Readonly with a lock and visible reason. Include a separate object reference 'Forest_Ruins / Beacon · Edit world' with locate and picker buttons. Missing never looks like Empty.

Bottom middle: '05 Color & gradient'. A real compact color popover with saturation/value square, hue bar, checkerboard alpha strip, labeled RGBA and HEX values. Explicit 'sRGB display' label; a separate HDR Intensity numeric field, not alpha. Beneath it, an amber-to-teal gradient with distinct color-stop and alpha-stop handles; selected stop position '0.35', swatch, and 'Linear' interpolation dropdown.

Bottom right: '06 Curves & ranges'. A compact 'Size over lifetime' curve editor with labeled axes 'Normalized age' and 'Size', 0-to-1 horizontal scale, three keys, one selected key with two tangent handles. Selected key fields 'Time 0.50', 'Value 0.80', 'Interpolation Bezier'. Below: a minimum/maximum range control, a numeric slider with its value field, and a small Reset action. Curves are UI examples, not scientific data.

Use the existing palette: #171A1F canvas, #1D2128 panels, #252B34 raised surfaces, #14171B inputs, #E6EAF0 primary text, #A4ADB9 secondary text, #5EC8BF accent; warning amber, error soft pink, source information muted blue. Small legible English labels, tabular numbers, dense 28px property-row rhythm. Independent specimen popovers may be visible simultaneously. Do not draw Shader Graph or a central global document-tab strip. No marketing copy, dashboard statistics, giant headings, glass, neon glow, perspective, or app-window mockup frame. Preserve the established nara emblem style rather than inventing a new mascot.
correction_prompts: Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit only one short label in this existing nara component atlas. In panel 02 Field states, the bottom legend currently reads 'Source override (takes precedence)'. Change that legend to exactly 'Source override', removing the parenthesized words. Keep its blue diamond icon and the separate Unsaved document legend. Preserve every other control, word, number, layout, color, curve, gradient, icon, size, and sharp typography exactly as they are. In particular preserve the invalid input '12..5', its error state, all mixed values, reference states and the entire other five specimens. Return the complete same-size full atlas, no crop, no redesign.

Landscape 3:2, straight-on, crisp industrial desktop-tool detail. Small heading 'nara / navigation & feedback' and 'Graphite · 0.4'. Six independent specimens in a tight 3-column by 2-row grid, thin separators, restrained corners, compact 13px-style typography and realistic 28px rows. This is a component specimen board, not one screen with six simultaneous dialogs.

Top left: '01 Hierarchy & selection'. A compact dock-group strip with 'Hierarchy' left-aligned inside this specimen only. Search field, scope 'Forest_Ruins · Edit world', nested rows Environment > Stone Arch, Beacon, Player > Camera. Beacon and Stone Arch selected with teal fill and left selection markers; keyboard focus separately outlined on Player. One selected object is hidden by the filter, as stated in the footer. Include one clear insertion-line drag example with a small 'Move under Environment' preview. Visibility and lock columns align. Footer '3 selected · 1 hidden' with 'Reveal'.

Top middle: '02 Tables & filters'. An Assets table with search 'arch', two removable filter chips 'Type: Mesh' and 'Folder: Environment', Clear filters, and result count. Columns Name, Type, Size, Status, with a visible sort arrow and resizable column dividers. Five realistically named rows; selected row stays distinguishable from hover; one row says Importing and another Missing. A small grid/list segmented switch belongs to this view, not to the outer docking system.

Top right: '03 Commands & menus'. Two independent specimens. A compact context menu with Duplicate Ctrl+D, Rename F2, Restore type default, Restore prefab source, a disabled Apply to source with reason 'Source is read-only', and Delete separated below. Under it a command palette with query 'frame', a visible invocation context 'Scene · Forest_Ruins · 2 objects', and results Frame selection / Frame all / Frame active camera. Show real keyboard hints Enter and Esc, not invented shortcut rows.

Bottom left: '04 Typed picker'. A usable asset-selection popover labeled 'Select Mesh', type filter Mesh, search input, breadcrumb 'Assets / Environment', four detailed stone-arch and beacon mesh thumbnails with names, one selected candidate, and a small preview/details area. Bottom buttons Cancel and Select; a separate small 'None' option is clearly labeled optional. Selection preview is distinct from confirmation.

Bottom middle: '05 Tasks & recoverable states'. A compact task list with three different entries: 'Import textures' Running with a progress bar 68% and Cancel; 'Build Windows' Queued; 'Generate collision' Failed with a reason and Retry/View log actions. Below, three small independent state specimens: 'Folder is empty' + Import, 'No matching assets' + Clear filters, 'Could not read folder' + Retry. Use compact inline messages and recognizable icons rather than large illustrations.

Bottom right: '06 Save & conflict'. A practical modal specimen 'Unsaved changes' listing two named documents, a pending-input warning 'Beacon / Range has invalid input' with 'Go to field', and disabled 'Save and close' with the reason clearly linked to the invalid field. Footer offers 'Continue editing' and an explicitly worded 'Discard changes…' secondary action. A separate slim notification below reads 'External changes detected' with Review; retained diagnostics are implied by a 'View details' action.

Use #171A1F, #1D2128, #252B34, #14171B with #E6EAF0 and #A4ADB9 text and #5EC8BF accents. Errors soft pink, warnings amber. Only meaningful accent areas; no glowing full-panel borders. Tabs align at each owning group's left edge. Include tiny practical icons, scrollbars, clear separators and true content density. No Shader Graph, no global centered resource tabs, no huge SaaS cards, no perspective or decorative background. Keep text concise and professionally readable.
